elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered language grants Client only a licence ("TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services"); no sentence vests ownership of Support Services results/work product in Client.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; Section 4 and the new sentence contain no "assigns" grant.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 2(d): "Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services" — the results licence covers whatever TrueLink IP is embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Credit Data clause still reads as a grant from Client to TrueLink and contains no affirmative statement that Client owns/retains all right, title and interest in Credit Data; narrowing the grant does not state retention.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Rewritten Section 8(d): "license to process Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services to Client" — the distribute/resell/exploit rights are removed.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no joint-ownership language exists in the cited or rendered text; Section 2(d) keeps the Interface with TrueLink and the new sentence is a one-way licence, so nothing creates co-ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 2(d) is left untouched: "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services for Client's business."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Word "irrevocable" appears in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Word "worldwide" appears in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Word "royalty-free" appears in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services for Client's business" — use and modify both present, business-purpose scope stated.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense all results of the Support Services for Client's business".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 8(d) now grants only the right "to process Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services to Client"; the prior "distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" rights are struck.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same operative rewrite of Section 8(d) satisfies this element at the preferred level as well.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the untouched Section 2(d) supplies the vendor tools/know-how ownership element, the inserted sentence supplies all five licence modifiers plus use, modify and sublicense for Client's business, and the rewritten Section 8(d) confines TrueLink's Credit Data rights to processing solely to provide the Hosting and Support Services.

Preferred level is not reached (and is not claimed): there is no ownership vesting in Client, no assignment of Support Services work product, and no affirmative statement that Client retains all rights in Credit Data. If the team later pushes to preferred, add (i) "All results and work product of the Support Services are works made for hire owned by Client, and TrueLink hereby assigns all right, title and interest therein to Client" and (ii) "As between the parties, Client retains all right, title and interest in and to Credit Data."

Minimality holds: only two operations, both inside the target elements; the favourable Non-Competition Agreement limitation and the whole of Section 4 and Section 2(d) survive verbatim, and no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra remedy has been bolted on. The insertion of a wholly new licence sentence is acceptable because no deliverables licence existed to amend.

Intent preserved: TrueLink's Interface ownership, the Support Services staffing mechanic, and the Non-Competition Agreement cross-reference are all intact, and nothing retained contradicts the narrowed data grant or the new licence.

Drafting check before sending: confirm "Hosting Services" is a defined term in this Agreement (the resolved definitions list only Client and TrueLink). If the contract instead uses a different label (e.g. the Section 3 hosting obligations or "Services"), conform the wording so the narrowed grant does not turn on an undefined term.

Optional tightening, not required for the fallback: "results of the Support Services" is the right hook here, but consider adding "including all deliverables, code, configurations and documentation delivered under Section 4" only if TrueLink resists scope — as drafted it would be an extra and would cost minimality.
